_purpose: Per-file map for the assistant: what each file is for, what it takes in, what it gives out, what it handles. Consult this instead of re-reading the codebase; update it whenever a file is created, changed or removed.
_rules: One entry per tracked file, keyed by path from the repository root.
inputs/outputs describe data that crosses the file boundary, not internal details.
Remove an entry in the same commit that deletes the file.
If an entry disagrees with the file, the file wins - then fix the entry.

structure.Docs/: Binding rules, reasoning log, reference, research, secrets. No code.
structure.Plan/: Architecture, roadmap, format spec, open questions. Decisions before code.
structure.Tests/: Test code (unit, integration, bench) and the permanent record of every run.
structure.Actions/: Workflow triggers, inputs, and committed outputs. No artifacts are used.
structure.internels/: Non-public helper material; skills are one markdown file each.
structure.examples/: Small runnable examples, empty until there is an API.
structure..github/workflows/: CI definitions. Each workflow is started by editing its trigger file.

.github/workflows/npm.yml.purpose: Packs the signpost, installs the tarball into a scratch project, and proves the failure behaviour on Linux/Windows/macOS x node 18/20.
outputs: CI records committed back to the branch
.github/workflows/npm.yml.handles: Tests the packed tarball rather than the working tree: a wrong `files` list would ship no bin, which is the failure this job exists to catch.

.github/workflows/scale.yml.purpose: The 1M-parameter scale test on three runners: train, record, assert the numbers, hand-test the CLI, keep the recording as an artifact, commit the facts.
.github/workflows/scale.yml.handles: Linux runs 150 steps as the reference and uploads the artifact; Windows and macOS run 40. The assertion step reads the transcript for the hand-test summary, so a CLI regression fails the job. Artifacts come from Bench/out/, not /tmp: upload-artifact cannot scandir the packaging sandbox's temp directory.

.github/workflows/tests.yml.purpose: Runner check matrix (ubuntu, windows, macos) that records each environment and commits results.
outputs: Actions/out/test-runs/*.json and *.junit.xml committed to the branch
.github/workflows/tests.yml.handles: Matrix of 3 (under the 5-runner cap), contents: write, no artifacts.

.gitignore.purpose: Keeps build noise and binary recordings out of git, with a narrow exception for tiny CI outputs.

Actions/README.md.purpose: Folder README: layout and rules for CI inputs and committed outputs.
Actions/README.md.handles: No artifacts, no Actions API reads.

Actions/in/README.md.purpose: Inputs folder rule: fixtures and matrices only, never written by a run.

Actions/scripts/commit_results.sh.purpose: Commits Actions/out/ and Actions/triggers/ back into the branch from a workflow runner.
inputs: whatever the job wrote under Actions/out
outputs: a commit on the branch, or nothing when there is nothing to commit
Actions/scripts/commit_results.sh.handles: Up to six runners share one branch since the npm workflow exists, so this retries eight times with jittered backoff and rebases explicitly. Safe to rebase because the only thing a job changes here is its own record file.

Actions/scripts/env_probe.py.purpose: Writes one JSON describing the runner (OS, Python, CPU, refs) to prove all three runners work and can commit.
Actions/scripts/env_probe.py.handles: Reads GITHUB_* environment variables; writes nothing else.

Actions/scripts/run_tests.py.purpose: Run pytest and write a machine-readable record of the run.
Actions/scripts/run_tests.py.handles: Captures exit code, counts (parsed from the dot line), versions, commit and output tails; writes one JSON per runner.

Actions/triggers/README.md.purpose: How trigger files start workflows, and why.

Actions/triggers/npm.txt.purpose: Trigger file for the npm-signpost workflow.
outputs: an npm CI run on three runners

Actions/triggers/scale.txt.purpose: Trigger file for the 1M-parameter scale workflow; editing it is how that run is started.
inputs: a dated line describing what the next run is for
Actions/triggers/scale.txt.handles: One line per run, newest last, so the file is also a short log of why each scale run happened.

Actions/triggers/tests.txt.purpose: Trigger file for .github/workflows/tests.yml; editing it starts a run.
outputs: a workflow run; last line echoed into the log

Bench/README.md.purpose: Index of the measurement scripts and the claim each one measures.
Bench/README.md.handles: Orientation for Bench/; points at Docs/Research.json for results.

Bench/claim01_error_vs_ratio.py.purpose: Claim 1: error vs compression ratio per encoder on three delta shapes.
Bench/claim01_error_vs_ratio.py.handles: Shapes: sparse 1%, dense small, rank-4 structure.

Bench/claim02_sparse_vs_lowrank.py.purpose: Claim 2: smallest encoder per density, both at any error and at exactness.
Bench/claim02_sparse_vs_lowrank.py.handles: The two columns are the finding: lossy and exact answers differ below full density.

Bench/claim03_anchor_spacing.py.purpose: Claim 3: chained-delta error as a function of anchor spacing.
inputs: a synthetic model and a sweep of anchor intervals
Bench/claim03_anchor_spacing.py.handles: Shows where accumulated delta error stops being acceptable, which is what sets the anchor interval.

Bench/claim04_long_run.py.purpose: Claim 4, second half: the cost of a recording over a long run.
inputs: a 1000-step run, with and without a coarse checkpoint interval
Bench/claim04_long_run.py.handles: Answers the long-run half of claim 4; the short sweep is claim04_storage_vs_checkpoints.py. Both numbers are published even where checkpoints win.

Bench/claim04_storage_vs_checkpoints.py.purpose: Claim 4, first half: recording versus checkpointing at matched accuracy.
Bench/claim04_storage_vs_checkpoints.py.handles: States the comparison so it cannot flatter the product: matched accuracy, not matched step count.

Bench/claim05_overhead.py.purpose: Claim 5: what recording costs per step, against the same loop with no recorder.
outputs: median step time, bytes written, stored/skipped counts
Bench/claim05_overhead.py.handles: Measurement only. The adapter-level version lives in the torch integration test.

Bench/claim06_adaptive_vs_fixed.py.purpose: Claim 6: the phase-adaptive policy versus a fixed interval at equal storage.
inputs: the same run recorded by both policies
Bench/claim06_adaptive_vs_fixed.py.handles: Compares usefulness per byte, not bytes; reports the case where fixed wins (a single-jump run) as well as where adaptive does.

Bench/claim07_hook_reach.py.purpose: Claim 7: what an optimizer step hook can reach, and what one log() call adds.
inputs: a bare hook attachment, then the same run with loss and data logged
Bench/claim07_hook_reach.py.handles: Draws the boundary of "attach in one line": the hook sees weights and gradients, not the loss or the batch.

Bench/claim08_torch_versions.py.purpose: Claim 8: does the plain-torch adapter depend on a torch version, and where is the floor?
inputs: the installed torch, plus the recorded matrix
Bench/claim08_torch_versions.py.handles: Evidence for the supported-version floor instead of an assurance; register_step_post_hook is the mechanism under test.

Bench/claim11_codecs.py.purpose: Claim 11-12 bench: storage ratio, exactness and CRC per data type, plus the dictionary comparison that justified removing `text-dict`.
inputs: synthetic prose, code, token-id arrays, pixel arrays and float weights
Bench/claim11_codecs.py.handles: Chooses nothing itself - it measures `choose_data_codec` + `encode_shard`/`decode_shard` and reports what they did. `--dictionary` re-runs the losing comparison.

Bench/claim13_capture_levels.py.purpose: Claim 13-14 bench: recorder overhead per data level, charged to log()+step(), and a join round-trip checked against the bytes.
inputs: a tiny torch model, synthetic batches, four data levels
outputs: a printed per-level table and join report
Bench/claim13_capture_levels.py.handles: Keeps the optimizer out of the timed region (timing it measured AdamW instead of the recorder). Reports the catch-up tail separately, and verifies every shard by re-decoding it rather than trusting the header.

Bench/claim15_activations.py.purpose: Claim 15: the cost of tier 3 (forward pass and whole step) plus a detection probe on a deliberately sick model.
inputs: a synthetic 4-block stack, with and without activations
Bench/claim15_activations.py.handles: Times the forward with no writer thread running; the first version timed step() too and reported +208% then +503% for the same code.

Bench/claim_arch_sweep.py.purpose: Phase 4.5: one recorder over six architectures with no model-specific code.
inputs: transformer, CNN, LSTM, state-space, mixture-of-experts and multi-tower models
Bench/claim_arch_sweep.py.handles: Tests that nothing in the adapter or recorder needs to know what the model is; also covered by Tests/integration/test_arch_sweep.py.

Bench/claim_plane_shuffle.py.purpose: Does byte-plane shuffling help? Measured, not assumed.
Bench/claim_plane_shuffle.py.handles: Result: hurts sparse, barely helps dense, identity on all-zero.

Bench/phase09_end_to_end.py.purpose: The v1.0 end-to-end proof: a transformer, a CNN and an RNN trained, recorded and measured.
Bench/phase09_end_to_end.py.handles: Anchors exact, chained error, weight-bytes-vs-checkpoint at matched resolution, and a same-seed A/B that proves recording changes nothing.

Bench/scale_1m_parameters.py.purpose: Scale test: train and record a 1,004,176-parameter causal transformer, then answer the product's questions from the file alone, and optionally hand-test the shipped CLI on it.
outputs: Bench/out/transformer-1m.archx.mdl (the recording, uploaded as an artifact)
stdout: parameters, loss, recording size, rebuild error, per-stored-step ratio, dead/saturated units
Bench/scale_1m_parameters.py.handles: Parameter budget swept with real count_parameters, never computed by hand (the first shape was 25% over). Both size ratios are printed with the denominator named, because the like-for-like number is per stored step. --hand-test runs the CLI as a subprocess and asserts on its text.

Bench/scale_deep_trace.py.purpose: Checks dense per-example tracing on a 1M model in GitHub Actions
Bench/scale_deep_trace.py.handles: Checks 1M states, example bytes, bitwise gradient round trips, SGD updates and same-input compression savings.

Docs/Change.md.purpose: Inbox for user-requested additions and changes, each with an effect on the roadmap.
outputs: roadmap edits or a documented decline

Docs/Changelog.md.purpose: What each version shipped and what changed between versions.

Docs/Deep_Recording.md.purpose: Explains dense history, trace setup, limits and costs
Docs/Deep_Recording.md.handles: Distinguishes local gradients from causal influence and explains storage and metadata limitations.

Docs/Files_Info.json.purpose: This file: the per-file map used instead of re-reading the codebase.
inputs: the current tree and each file's role
outputs: purpose, inputs, outputs, handles per path
Docs/Files_Info.json.handles: Must be updated in the same change that adds or edits a file.

Docs/Logic.md.purpose: Call chains from a user entry point down to files, plus failure paths.
Docs/Logic.md.handles: Breakage tracing. Updated whenever a call chain changes.

Docs/README.md.purpose: Folder README for Docs/: what belongs here and what does not.
Docs/README.md.handles: Points each kind of document at its home folder.

Docs/Research.json.purpose: Every lookup that influenced a decision, with sources and verdict.
Docs/Research.json.handles: Prevents re-researching the same thing. Sources are GitHub API URLs because raw and docs hosts are blocked.

Docs/Rules.md.purpose: The binding working rules: structure, process, testing, CI workaround, environment limits.
Docs/Rules.md.handles: Must be read before any change. Numbered rules are referenced from other docs.

Docs/Secrets.md.purpose: Exact name and purpose of every GitHub Actions secret the project needs.
outputs: names the user sets in repository settings
Docs/Secrets.md.handles: The assistant never sets a secret; names must match character for character.

Docs/Technical.md.purpose: Technical reference: stack, repository layout, per-file roles, glossary, environment facts.

Docs/Thinking.md.purpose: Reasoning log: why something was built or changed, what broke, how it was split and solved.
inputs: problems met during a round of work
Docs/Thinking.md.handles: Decision history. Updated after every round.

Docs/Workaround.md.purpose: Environment limitations and the exact workaround for each.
inputs: failures caused by the sandbox, token or runner limits
Docs/Workaround.md.handles: Rust toolchain, Actions logs, raw.githubusercontent.com, heavy installs, runner cap, binary recordings.

Docs/activation_results.json.purpose: The recorded tier-3 numbers: added cost per forward, batch-scaling plateau, and the detection probe.
outputs: the cost figures cited in Plan/Roadmap.md and Docs/Research.json
Docs/activation_results.json.handles: Generated output, committed so the overhead claim is checkable.

Docs/capture_levels.json.purpose: The recorded Claim 13-14 numbers: per-level bytes, median/p95/max step cost, catch-up share, seal time, and the join report with verified-shard counts.
Docs/capture_levels.json.handles: Generated output, committed so the overhead claim is checkable.

Docs/codec_results.json.purpose: The recorded Claim 11-12 table: per-case raw/stored bytes, ratio, chosen codec, exactness and CRC agreement.
outputs: claimed numbers cited in Plan/Roadmap.md and Docs/Research.json
Docs/codec_results.json.handles: Generated output, committed so a reader can check a claim without rerunning the bench.

Docs/phase09_results.json.purpose: Committed numbers for the Phase 9 work (adapter breadth and the end-to-end proof).
Docs/phase09_results.json.handles: A record, not a source: the benches produce it, the changelog cites it.

Docs/torch_matrix.json.purpose: Which torch versions were actually exercised, and what each could record.
outputs: the supported-version floor quoted in the changelog
Docs/torch_matrix.json.handles: Version claims are read from here rather than from the intent to support them.

Plan/Architecture.md.purpose: The decided design: observer model, adapters per setup, storage, tiers, non-goals, risks.
outputs: scope the roadmap is derived from
Plan/Architecture.md.handles: Every decision is marked DECIDED (mine to defend) or ASK (user's).

Plan/Format_Spec.md.purpose: Normative byte-level specification of the .archx.mdl container (format 1.0, draft).
outputs: header, block, payload, footer layouts and reader rules
Plan/Format_Spec.md.handles: Frozen by roadmap step 1.1; code must match it or the spec is amended.

Plan/Open_Questions.md.purpose: Decisions waiting on the user, with recommendation and evidence.
inputs: ambiguities found while writing the plan
Plan/Open_Questions.md.handles: Unanswered question means the dependent step is not started.

Plan/Origin_Chat.md.purpose: Durable extraction of the user's origin conversation: pipeline lineage, format wishlist, requirements the later brief omitted, and where the two disagree.
outputs: requirement changes in Plan/ and Docs/Change.md
Plan/Origin_Chat.md.handles: Replaces the raw chat as a reference; the raw chat is never committed.

Plan/README.md.purpose: Folder README: what belongs in Plan/ and what does not.

Plan/Roadmap.md.purpose: Ordered work list by phase and version; one step at a time.
outputs: what to build next and its acceptance test
Plan/Roadmap.md.handles: Status column is the source of truth for progress.

README.md.purpose: Entry point: what the product is, status, and where to start reading.
README.md.handles: Orientation only. Points to Plan/Architecture.md and Docs/Rules.md.

Tests/README.md.purpose: Folder README: test layers, when each runs, where records go.

Tests/Records/README.md.purpose: Naming, shape and retention rules for recorded test runs.
Tests/Records/README.md.handles: Version folders; keep current plus two.

Tests/integration/test_arch_sweep.py.purpose: Integration: six architectures record through one adapter and reach the same tier.
outputs: pass/fail, and the per-architecture tier in the assertion message
Tests/integration/test_arch_sweep.py.handles: The regression guard for Bench/claim_arch_sweep.py; skips when torch is absent.

Tests/integration/test_cli_activations.p.purpose: The two tier-3 CLI commands through `python -m archx`: demo output, refusal to overwrite, JSON shape, filters, and the no-activations explanation.
inputs: a real recording made by `archx demo`
Tests/integration/test_cli_activations.p.handles: Uses the real entry point, because the contract a user has is the command and its exit code.

Tests/integration/test_container_end_to_.purpose: Integration: writer -> crash -> recovery -> reader -> CLI as one flow, including a real SIGKILLed subprocess.
Tests/integration/test_container_end_to_.handles: Proves the modules still agree when wired together.

Tests/integration/test_crash_recovery.py.purpose: Integration: kill a training process mid-run, then recover its history from the file.
inputs: a child process running a real recorder
Tests/integration/test_crash_recovery.py.handles: That a crash costs the step in flight and not the history, that data written before the kill survives, and that recovering a copy leaves the evidence untouched.

Tests/integration/test_end_to_end_proof..purpose: Pins the v1.0 promises on three real trainings.
Tests/integration/test_end_to_end_proof..handles: Bit-identical results, exact anchors, tier 2 with gaps named, unstored steps answerable, data joined to the weights it moved.

Tests/integration/test_example_gradients.purpose: Exercises dense weight history and per-example gradients
Tests/integration/test_example_gradients.handles: Checks full-history examples, bitwise trace fidelity, text, old/new blocks, corruption, crash recovery and bounded trace backlog.

Tests/integration/test_file_map.py.purpose: Integration: Docs/Files_Info.json lists every tracked file, describes nothing that was deleted, and gives each entry the four fields its own rules require.
Tests/integration/test_file_map.py.handles: The map's instruction to update itself is now a test rather than a habit; it listed 126 of 170 tracked files before this existed.

Tests/integration/test_format_spec_match.purpose: Parses real files against Plan/Format_Spec.md so the spec cannot drift.
Tests/integration/test_format_spec_match.handles: Registry byte layout, anchor body, delta prefix, every JSON block's documented keys, and a rebuild using the spec alone.

Tests/integration/test_forward_compat.py.purpose: Integration: a file written by a newer minor version is read with a warning, and a newer major is refused naming both versions.
inputs: hand-built headers with a bumped format version
Tests/integration/test_forward_compat.py.handles: The rule is also written in Plan/Format_Spec.md; this is the test that keeps the rule and the reader in step.

Tests/integration/test_hf_adapter.py.purpose: Proves the HF adapter against a real Trainer: steps, weights, loss parity, accumulation, ranks.
Tests/integration/test_hf_adapter.py.handles: Skips with a stated reason when transformers/accelerate are absent; the CI workflow installs them so the tests run rather than skip.

Tests/integration/test_hook_reach.py.purpose: Integration: what the optimizer hook alone records, and what log() adds.

Tests/integration/test_join.py.purpose: Integration: the join - this data moved these weights at these steps - from the file alone.
Tests/integration/test_join.py.handles: The product's core claim, asserted through the container rather than the recorder.

Tests/integration/test_join_round_trip.p.purpose: Claim 14 as a test: the file alone answers which data, at which step, and what movement - with every shard re-decoded and hash-verified.
inputs: a recorded .archx.mdl from a toy model at each data level
Tests/integration/test_join_round_trip.p.handles: Also covers JOIN_INCOMPLETE, unsynced_log, and the effect_step invariant (movement must land on a step the file actually holds).

Tests/integration/test_launcher.py.purpose: Proves the launcher records a real script and fails loudly when it cannot.
Tests/integration/test_launcher.py.handles: Runs real subprocesses; pins the three silent failures (torch not importable, AdamW has no step, a broken sitecustomize is ignored).

Tests/integration/test_lightning_adapter.purpose: Proves the Lightning adapter against a real pl.Trainer.
Tests/integration/test_lightning_adapter.handles: Compares every reconstructed step against the weights observed at the matching batch end, which is what caught the off-by-one-update store point.

Tests/integration/test_npm_signpost.py.purpose: Runs the signpost from pytest: install shape, loud failure, --version parity, and the node suite.
Tests/integration/test_npm_signpost.py.handles: Skips with a stated reason when node is absent - never fakes a pass, since the whole point is that a wrong install cannot look like a working one.

Tests/integration/test_recovery_property.purpose: Property test over 8 seeds: any tear point leaves a valid, ordered prefix and a rebuilt index that matches.
Tests/integration/test_recovery_property.handles: Documents that a tear inside META loses META but never corrupts it.

Tests/integration/test_torch_adapter.py.purpose: Integration: a real nn.Module and SGD, attached, read back, and timed.
Tests/integration/test_torch_adapter.py.handles: Reconstruction, numerics unchanged with the same seed, the join after a real optimizer step, tier reporting, and the overhead budget. Skips with a reason when torch is absent.

Tests/unit/cli/test_cli.py.purpose: Unit tests for the CLI surface through the real entry point.
Tests/unit/cli/test_cli.py.handles: --version/help exit codes, info JSON, broken-file error path, recover.

Tests/unit/container/test_reader.py.purpose: Unit tests for hostile/damaged files: foreign magic, newer major, bit flip, absurd length, torn tail, unknown block type.
Tests/unit/container/test_reader.py.handles: Each test asserts a specific typed error.

Tests/unit/container/test_recovery.py.purpose: Unit tests for recovery: whole blocks kept, index rebuilt, copy mode, no-op on healthy files.
Tests/unit/container/test_recovery.py.handles: Crash is simulated by truncation, SIGKILL is covered in integration.

Tests/unit/container/test_schema.py.purpose: Unit tests for struct sizes and CRC placement.
Tests/unit/container/test_schema.py.handles: Header 40, block 28, footer 56; header CRC over bytes 0..19, footer over 0..47.

Tests/unit/container/test_values.py.purpose: Unit tests for reading a recording back as values, events and ties.
Tests/unit/container/test_values.py.handles: That reconstruction matches live weights within the encoder budget and that tied names come back identical.

Tests/unit/container/test_writer.py.purpose: Unit tests for the writer: roundtrip, real compression, abort behaviour.
Tests/unit/container/test_writer.py.handles: Proves stored_len < raw_len for compressible input and that abort leaves no footer.

Tests/unit/data/test_activations.py.purpose: 12 tests: exact statistics, forward accumulation, stride sampling, non-finite handling, the layer cap, tier 3 end to end, and that recording changes no number.
inputs: synthetic tensors and a real recorded run
Tests/unit/data/test_activations.py.handles: Asserts the sampled mean stays close to the exact mean on a tensor whose halves differ wildly - the case a truncating sample gets wrong.

Tests/unit/data/test_capture.py.purpose: Unit tests for data capture: dedup, levels, sensitivity, caps, codecs, exact round-trip.
Tests/unit/data/test_capture.py.handles: That an epoch over the same data costs no new bytes, that observe does no expensive work, and that every shipped codec is lossless.

Tests/unit/data/test_codecs.py.purpose: Unit tests for shard codecs: lossless round-trip, CRC identity, varint boundaries, realistic-token detection, incompressible honesty, and the absence of the removed dictionary codec.
inputs: synthetic shard payloads of each supported shape
Tests/unit/data/test_codecs.py.handles: Asserts that a codec which cannot compress (pixels, weights) says so with a ratio near or above 1 instead of pretending.

Tests/unit/encoders/test_encoders.py.purpose: Unit tests for the encoders: exactness where promised, measured error elsewhere.
Tests/unit/encoders/test_encoders.py.handles: Also pins the measured shuffle behaviour so the finding cannot silently regress.

Tests/unit/encoders/test_quantization_pa.purpose: Unit: int16 quantization is offered only where its error fits the budget, and decodes back at the right width.
inputs: synthetic tensors at several reconstruction budgets
Tests/unit/encoders/test_quantization_pa.handles: Watches the defect where an int16 delta was decoded as int8 and came back at half length.

Tests/unit/formats/test_registry.py.purpose: Unit tests for the tensor registry: stable indices, tie groups, prefixes.
Tests/unit/formats/test_registry.py.handles: That tied weights are one storage unit and that region/component labels use the longest matching prefix.

Tests/unit/test_capabilities.py.purpose: Unit: the tier ladder, the reasons attached to missing fields, and the rule that a tier's description names only fields that tier records.
inputs: fields offered and denied in various orders
Tests/unit/test_capabilities.py.handles: Includes the guard that tier 3's prose cannot get ahead of the blocks - it promised eval results for every release without an adapter that produced any.

Tests/unit/test_parallel_detection.py.purpose: Sharded models are recognised and refused, on stubbed engines.
Tests/unit/test_parallel_detection.py.handles: FSDP/ZeRO/TP names, nested wrappers, absent and meta parameters, hostile objects, and the allow_partial file telling the truth about itself.

Tests/unit/test_policy.py.purpose: Unit tests for the phase policy: phases, triggers, heartbeat, anchors.
Tests/unit/test_policy.py.handles: That density follows the stage of the run and that explicit events win over the phase.

Tests/unit/test_reconstruction_guarantee.purpose: Unit: exact at anchors, float32 rounding between them, and the anchor spacing that guarantee depends on.
inputs: a small model recorded with and without forced anchor spacing
Tests/unit/test_reconstruction_guarantee.handles: The two halves of the promise are asserted separately, because reporting only one of them would overstate or understate what a step gives you.

Tests/unit/test_recorder.py.purpose: Unit tests for the recorder: observation, no mutation, degradation, observations written.
Tests/unit/test_recorder.py.handles: That the recorder never alters a weight, never raises into training, drops detail under backpressure, and writes what it promised into the file.

archx/__init__.py.purpose: Public package surface; exposes __version__ and FORMAT_VERSION only.

archx/__main__.py.purpose: `python -m archx`, the same CLI as the `archx` script.
archx/__main__.py.handles: Exists so the tool works from a clone without an editable install on PATH; no logic of its own.

archx/_launcher_hook.py.purpose: The injected sitecustomize: patches torch optimizers once torch.optim loads.
archx/_launcher_hook.py.handles: Installed via sys.meta_path because torch is not importable at start-up; wraps every optimizer class that defines its own step because AdamW does not define one; never raises into the user's training job.

archx/adapters/__init__.py.purpose: Marks the adapters package; one file per framework.
archx/adapters/__init__.py.handles: Nothing at import time: torch is optional.

archx/adapters/example_gradients.py.purpose: Opt-in lossless per-example local gradient encoder and reader
archx/adapters/example_gradients.py.handles: Validates batch-gradient sums and losslessly encodes/decodes raw, shuffled or sparse example gradients and packed examples, retaining legacy block support.

archx/adapters/hf.py.purpose: Hugging Face Trainer: one callback, no fork of the training loop.
archx/adapters/hf.py.handles: Gradients and learning rate read at on_pre_optimizer_step (the norm is the CLIPPED one when max_grad_norm > 0), the step taken at on_optimizer_step keyed on state.global_step, model unwrapped so no 'module.' prefix reaches the file, and only the main process records. No optimizer hook is registered: it raises AttributeError on accelerate's AcceleratedOptimizer. The loss is observed via loss_hook or callback.log, never taken from on_log.

archx/adapters/lightning.py.purpose: PyTorch Lightning: one callback, tier 1 with no user code.
archx/adapters/lightning.py.handles: Stores at on_train_batch_end (weights are new there) keyed on trainer.global_step, which advances only on a real update; gradient norm and lr are cached at on_before_optimizer_step, where the weights are still old. Loss comes free from outputs['loss'].

archx/adapters/torch.py.purpose: Raw PyTorch: attach in one line via optimizer.register_step_post_hook.
archx/adapters/torch.py.handles: Global gradient norm read before zero_grad(), tied parameters kept via remove_duplicate=False, and the batch converted in exactly one place.

archx/capabilities.py.purpose: What a run could actually see: the tier reached and every field it could not see.
outputs: capabilities_missing with a reason per field
archx/capabilities.py.handles: A tier is measured, never requested; a tier cannot be reached above a missing lower tier. TIER_MEANING names only fields the build records - tier 3 promised eval results for every release without an adapter that produced any.

archx/cli/__init__.py.purpose: CLI package surface with a lazy import so `import archx` stays cheap.

archx/cli/activations.py.purpose: `archx activations`: print the layer summaries, and flag dead or saturated layers.
outputs: a table, JSON, or an explanation of why the file has no tier-3 data
archx/cli/activations.py.handles: A file below tier 3 exits 0 with the reason from its own capability block - absence is not an error, silence would be.

archx/cli/demo.py.purpose: `archx demo`: record a small run so a new install has a real file to inspect.
outputs: a recorded .archx.mdl and the commands to read it
archx/cli/demo.py.handles: Refuses to overwrite an existing file, and needs torch (says so and exits 1 without it).

archx/cli/diff.py.purpose: archx diff: what changed between two steps of one run, or between two recordings.
outputs: per-tensor movement, absolute and relative to each tensor's own size, by region
archx/cli/diff.py.handles: Compares store points only. Two files that share no tensor name report 'cannot compare' rather than the strongest verdict on zero comparisons, and the folded-update count is labelled as updates, not steps.

archx/cli/events.py.purpose: archx events: per-step observations, user annotations and data segments.
outputs: human table or JSON with steps / observations / annotations / segments
archx/cli/events.py.handles: Keeps the three streams apart, because they answer three different questions.

archx/cli/info.py.purpose: `archx info`: summarize a recording (format, size, closure, blocks, key META fields).
outputs: human or JSON text, exit code
archx/cli/info.py.handles: Reads metadata only; never loads tensor payloads.

archx/cli/main.py.handles: --version, info, recover; new commands are added as their modules land.

archx/cli/reconstruct.py.purpose: archx reconstruct: rebuild the weights at a step and write them to .npz.
archx/cli/reconstruct.py.handles: Defaults to the last stored step. Answers any step inside the recorded range, including steps between store points, and says which anchor the answer was rebuilt from. Refuses only a step outside the file, and names the range it does have.

archx/cli/recover.py.purpose: `archx recover`: close a crashed recording, in place or into a copy.

archx/container/__init__.py.purpose: Container package surface: Reader, Writer, BlockType, read_header.

archx/container/compress.py.purpose: Per-block compression: zstandard if installed, else stdlib compression.zstd (3.14+), else zlib/none.
archx/container/compress.py.handles: effective_codec() downgrades ZSTD to ZLIB when no zstd exists; NONE always works.

archx/container/reader.py.purpose: Validating reader: header checks, prefix CRCs, length caps, payload CRCs, footer detection, index decode.
archx/container/reader.py.handles: Refuses foreign files, newer majors, absurd lengths, bad CRCs; skips unknown block types; reports torn tails instead of trusting them.

archx/container/recovery.py.purpose: Rebuild a crashed file: keep whole blocks, truncate the tail, rebuild the index, append a footer.
archx/container/recovery.py.handles: Steps are read from block prefixes, so no decompression is needed; the capability block is the exception, and is recomputed from the surviving blocks because a crash happens before close. Only truncates and re-appends; never rewrites block bytes.

archx/container/schema.py.purpose: Byte-level layout: header/block/footer structs, block-type ids, codec ids, flag bits, CRC helpers.
archx/container/schema.py.handles: The only file where byte offsets live. Block prefix is 28 bytes: type, codec, flags, step, raw_len, payload_len, payload_crc, block_crc(over 0..23).

archx/container/values.py.purpose: Blocks turned back into meaning: registry, anchor, delta and the Timeline over them.
archx/container/values.py.handles: Decoding with the encoder the writer recorded, tie re-aliasing, and last-statement-wins for a segment that grew while the run continued.

archx/container/writer.py.purpose: Append-only block writer with batched fsync, index block and footer.
archx/container/writer.py.handles: Append-only block writing, CRCs, index, recovery flags, and smallest-of-candidate compression selection.

archx/data/__init__.py.purpose: Marks the data package: codecs and capture.

archx/data/activations.py.purpose: Tier 3: reduce each layer's forward-pass output to a fixed-size summary (mean, std, min/max, dead-unit and saturation fractions).
inputs: a tensor or tuple handed to a forward hook
outputs: one JSON-serialisable dict per layer per store point
archx/data/activations.py.handles: Never keeps a tensor: stride-samples above MAX_ELEMENTS so the cost is bounded by layer count, counts non-finite values instead of letting them poison the moments, and records how many forward passes were folded in.

archx/data/capture.py.purpose: Data capture in two phases: cheap observe on the training thread, seal off it.
outputs: Segment records with characteristics and per-region effects
archx/data/capture.py.handles: Four data levels, content dedup, sensitive shards, a cap that degrades to pointers, and a lock so the writer thread and the training thread cannot corrupt each other's view.

archx/data/codecs.py.purpose: Content id and per-shard codec: text-zstd, tokens-varint or zstd, all lossless.
inputs: bytes of one batch or shard
archx/data/codecs.py.handles: Content addressing and the measured varint threshold (ids < 128).

archx/encoders/base.py.purpose: Encoder contract, the Encoded result, and smallest-under-budget choice.
outputs: Encoded(encoding, body, nnz_or_rank, value_dtype, max_abs_error, rel_error)
archx/encoders/base.py.handles: relative_error() is the single definition of error used everywhere.

archx/encoders/dense.py.purpose: Encoding 2: symmetric int8/int16 quantization of a dense delta.
archx/encoders/dense.py.handles: Error is computed from the decoded array, not from pre-decode values.

archx/encoders/dense_raw.py.purpose: Encoding 4: the lossless fallback, raw (optionally shuffled) bytes through zstd.
archx/encoders/dense_raw.py.handles: Guarantees every tensor has an exact option; shuffle is opt-in because it measured badly.

archx/encoders/lowrank.py.purpose: Encoding 3: truncated SVD of a 2-D delta at the smallest rank meeting the error budget.
archx/encoders/lowrank.py.handles: Refuses non-2-D tensors and refuses noise, which is the honest behaviour.

archx/encoders/plane.py.purpose: Reversible byte-plane shuffle and XOR-against-previous helper.
archx/encoders/plane.py.handles: Measured to hurt zero-heavy data; used only where it helps.

archx/encoders/sparse.py.purpose: Encoding 1: index-gap + value compression for deltas with few moved entries.
archx/encoders/sparse.py.handles: Refuses when more than half the entries moved, because index cost then beats density.

archx/encoders/unchanged.py.handles: Tied and frozen parameters hit this every step.

archx/errors.py.purpose: Typed exceptions so callers can degrade selectively.

archx/formats/__init__.py.purpose: Format-level value types shared by file, encoders and reader.

archx/formats/dtype.py.purpose: The one-byte dtype ids from the spec mapped to numpy.
archx/formats/dtype.py.handles: bf16 is refused at decode (no numpy equivalent); everything else round-trips.

archx/formats/registry.py.purpose: The tensor registry: names, dtypes, shapes, tie groups, regions, components.
outputs: TensorEntry list addressed by stable index
archx/formats/registry.py.handles: Tied weights detected by data_ptr so bytes are stored once and the alias survives.

archx/launcher.py.purpose: `archx run -- <command>`: record a training script without editing it.
outputs: non-zero exit when nothing was captured
archx/launcher.py.handles: Copies _launcher_hook.py into a temp dir as sitecustomize.py, prepends it to PYTHONPATH, runs the command, then verifies the file really contains steps. Never leaves an empty recording behind.

archx/parallel.py.purpose: Recognise FSDP/ZeRO/TP wrappers and refuse to record a sharded model.
archx/parallel.py.handles: Class-name and parameter-shape detection that needs no deepspeed import and never raises; attach() refuses before opening a file unless allow_partial=True.

archx/policy.py.purpose: Phase policy: warmup / middle / cool-down plus event triggers -> store, skip or anchor.
archx/policy.py.handles: Recording density. Thresholds are per region, never global; a short run stays in warmup.

archx/recorder.py.purpose: The hook surface: takes a snapshot, decides, and hands work to the writer thread.
archx/recorder.py.handles: Queues snapshots, observations and traces; compares dense delta encodings, compresses independent trace blocks and applies trace backpressure without dropping records.

archx/version.py.purpose: Single source of version and format constants (MAGIC, END_MAGIC, FORMAT_MAJOR/MINOR).
archx/version.py.handles: Imported by schema, reader, writer and the CLI.

examples/README.md.purpose: Folder README: example contract (one folder, runs on CPU, writes its own recording).

examples/quickstart.py.purpose: The five-minute tour: record a small run, then answer all five product questions from the file alone.
outputs: printed answers plus a .archx.mdl the reader can inspect
examples/quickstart.py.handles: Compares the rebuilt weights against the live tensors, which is the only check that proves anything.

internels/README.md.purpose: Folder README: what non-public helper material is allowed here.
internels/README.md.handles: Nothing here is imported by the package.

internels/chat/README.md.purpose: Folder README for local-only chat exports: the rule, why they are kept, what is in here.
internels/chat/README.md.handles: Committed on purpose; the chat bodies next to it are not.

internels/skills/README.md.purpose: Skill file format: when to use, steps, pitfalls.
internels/skills/README.md.handles: Skills are added only when reused.

npm/archx/README.md.purpose: What the npm package is, how to install the real tool, and why the exit code is 1.
outputs: shown on the npm registry page
npm/archx/README.md.handles: Orientation for someone who arrived by the wrong package manager.

npm/archx/bin/archx.js.purpose: The whole signpost: prints the PyPI install command and docs link, exits 1 for any real use.
npm/archx/bin/archx.js.handles: No child_process, no Python, no pip shell-out. `npm i archx && archx train.py` must fail loudly rather than look like a working install.

npm/archx/package.json.purpose: The npm signpost package manifest: name `archx`, one bin, no dependencies, three published files.
npm/archx/package.json.handles: Declares no `os` restriction on purpose: a signpost must install on Windows too and explain itself there, rather than sending the user nowhere.

npm/archx/test/cli.test.js.purpose: 8 node tests for the signpost, including one that asserts the package cannot grow an implementation.
npm/archx/test/cli.test.js.handles: Run with `npm test` (node --test, no dependencies); the Python suite also invokes it.

pyproject.toml.purpose: Packaging: distribution `archx.mdl`, import `archx`, CLI `archx`, MIT, py>=3.10, deps numpy+zstandard.
pyproject.toml.handles: Version is duplicated in archx/version.py by design (build backend needs it statically); both move together at release.
